label: context.reference
description: Exact JSON/file-tool and artifact movement recipe for independent Tasks with nonblocking, verifier-aware Home returns.
text:
Home Task authoring is ordinary file effects and artifact movement. This artifact contains a worked example under authoring_examples; use artifact.read on this artifact for the full JSON. Example names are illustrative exact identities, not runtime-recognized labels or a reusable runtime template. Resolve actual paths, current descriptor bytes, tool ids, EE identity and interface ids from attested invocation metadata, bound artifacts, and granted file.read/file.list. Never copy example identities into a live Home.

1. INSPECT. Start from the bound authoring coordinates: Home receives artifact-home-delivery and standard Tasks receive artifact-run-authoring-coordinates for their exact run. Their authoring object lists registry/run/EE records, tool-id mappings and per-tool declared read/write/execute rules. Exact door overrides include concrete paths; host_binding_not_supplied explicitly means the machine path was not supplied. These coordinates do not add a grant. Read any model-visible composition affordance's current schema and use it when it prepares the required ordinary file/send effects; retain its actual receipts. For manual authoring, read the current run, its worker policy, the actual EE chain, the desired worker/provider/door descriptors and sidecars, the relevant tool descriptors and current run schema. Read existing Task records before deciding to create or continue one. Provider authentication remains private; do not read or copy credentials. Use the actual model catalog and provider policy. Distinguish installed registry/bundle paths from an explicitly granted source workspace and execution tool; a missing source/compiler is a capability gap, not permission to use the provider cwd. Choose an already permitted EE. Create a narrower project EE only when the goal needs that boundary and the granted path and policy allow it. An ordinary Task does not require a new EE.

2. AUTHOR EXACT OWNERS. Choose independent exact worker/provider/tool-door/client identities as needed for isolation, reusing code only by explicit owner imports. Copy the complete descriptor and required life/config sidecars from the installed reference; a driver reference does not import its configuration. A System worker pin has interface_type=system, role=worker and a policy.json ceiling, with no executable driver or life. That pin is the existing RuntimeRelay path. A zero-code role=system folder is inert and cannot substitute for it. The Task receive pin may be its worker pin. The return pin may be the existing exact Home worker pin already bound to Home, when that is the intended policy boundary. A separate return boundary needs its own permitted exact pin and explicit Home checkpoint; never infer parent callbacks from a run id.

3. POLICY IS REQUIRED DATA. Add each new exact id to every restrictive EE layer that must permit it and to the appropriate concrete worker ceiling, using only authorized file effects. Preserve unrelated entries. Null EE allowance is unrestricted at that layer; [] allows nothing. Never grant a provider family or interpret source_names as admission. The worker pin itself must be allowed by each EE layer. Every tool's interface and owning WEK must survive the worker ceiling and EE chain, and the tool door must be bound. Task authority comes from its EE position and own ceiling, not Home's initiating grant. Home can author a more capable Task only where existing authority permits the needed records; missing authority is an explicit gap, not a reason to edit arbitrary ancestors.

4. CONTEXT IS AUTHORED. Bind the complete role-artifact closure for the current worker and every exact worker relay surviving formation on every relevant checkpoint, as {id,access:{read:true}}. Formation fails when a required role is absent; it does not automatically attach it. Source ceiling roles describe their own workers and are not instructions for the recipient to become Home. Include the assignment, constraints, selected prior evidence and return contract explicitly. Extra knowledge is not inherited from a provider thread, ambient repository, initiating run, project label or memory profile.

5. FILE EFFECTS. Use the exact model-visible file writer from the formed tools. A new file uses content with expected_before_hash:null. Existing JSON edits use an observed expected_before_hash or expected_before_content so concurrent changes refuse rather than disappear. Hashes from file tools use their declared algorithm; do not substitute a guessed SHA hash. RFC 6902 patches also require expected_after_hash. A writes batch validates/stages before installation but is not an all-or-nothing cross-file transaction: inspect reported paths/hashes after an error. Write descriptors, policies and bound artifact payloads before making the receiving run frontier visible. Read back the installed bytes and fail closed if a dependency is missing. No file drop is delivery: writing run JSON never substitutes for artifact.send.

6. COMPOSE THE RUN. Use this bound artifact's run_record_schema.document, available in full through artifact.read. Its source path and SHA-256 identify this exact generated schema, including the status and nonblank trace constraints enforced by its stated validation_source. These source coordinates are provenance, not an ambient filesystem read grant. Cross-record and registry checks belong to the actual candidate validator. Author a nonempty trace on the run and every checkpoint, and list projected checkpoint ids in active_checkpoints. The Task input binds its exact worker receive pin and routes to its provider. Provider tool-call checkpoints bind the provider, carry tool.call.allowed with tool_call_allowed and params.tools containing only the exact tools at that door, and route to that door; tool results return on their own checkpoint to the provider. Provider checkpoint progression uses its distinct narrow file writer and source/door/result checkpoints from the installed provider/client contract. Preserve interface_state and unrelated projected checkpoints when updating a continuous run; use a new checkpoint id or epoch for a new generation, never rearm by changing unrelated JSON. Supply a real client interface/binding when the Task must be writable in Tasks; otherwise it is an honest read-only projection. Client sidecars belong to the client contract, not runtime ontology.

7. AUTHOR DISPATCH WITHOUT AUTOMATIC WORK. Home needs the Task receive pin in its permitted active authored surface, and the Task needs a projected input checkpoint on that same pin. An exact-name provider-output checkpoint with its exact provider inbound binding can carry an outbound binding for a model-selected artifact.send without forwarding every provider/tool artifact to the Task. The emitter's executing checkpoint and door must remain present and active during the send. Its fresh grant must include the target. artifact.send only targets a System interface; it is not a World-provider, chat or time-interface RPC. Send the concrete assignment after file verification. The result admitted/seq proves emission, not Task completion or even immediate consumption. An admitted outbound with no live reader remains durable and can catch up; do not duplicate work because the reader is temporarily absent. On a definite refusal repair the exact binding/policy and retry deliberately; on an uncertain outcome inspect the existing evidence before repeating a side effect.

8. RETURN WITHOUT BLOCKING HOME. Author the return address into the Task's active exact binding surface and ceiling and keep an independent Home checkpoint listening there. The worked example explicitly sends task.summary for every completed, blocked, or failed outcome, carrying status, summary and evidence. Its artifact_exists verifier with task.summary.received proves readable receipt only. That mark does not certify semantic completion. A real completion obligation instead names the actual evidence label, mark and verifier, such as coder.build.result -> build_success -> coder.build.ok where those contracts are granted. Verifier and mark names in the worked example are not installation guarantees. Inspect the declared registry/verifier and registry/mark child roots before referencing them. If artifact_exists, build_success, or the required outcome is absent, identify that missing package and author/install it through permitted file effects before using it; a tool-call-format verifier cannot certify a completed build. Requirements belong only to the checkpoint awaiting that evidence. Never attach Task completion to Home's operator-input checkpoint. Several independent Tasks may return through one intentionally shared Home pin; isolate them with separate exact pins when policy or receipt boundaries differ, never payload label routing. Receivers author a new generation for later outcomes after consuming a generation.

The example uses an explicit model-authored result send. An installed interface author may instead route its terminal provider output through an explicit return binding. In that case bind its actual success AND error artifact vocabulary, preserve authored output selection, and do not claim an implicit callback. Do not run both return paths for the same outcome. Return a meaningful result, source Task/run identity as content for attribution, exact artifact refs and required verification evidence. Home decides whether to deliver it outward. For checked_input_intake, notification_action controls unwrapped outcome arrivals: followup invokes the receiving model, while queue only stores context and does not start a response. The installed intake template explicitly selects followup for new receivers; existing concrete receiver configuration is preserved. Keep a passive queue only when no automatic interpretation is intended. Explicit provider.peer.message actions retain their declared meaning. Change a concrete intake declaration consistently in its interface and owned run state only when that intake has no pending input; never replay an already admitted outcome to manufacture a fresh notification. Do not copy the full Task trace or private reasoning into the user conversation or the live voice model.

9. TIME AND EVENTS. Inspect the installed world_cron activation contract and copy its complete exact interface/authoring/run topology with its own state. Existing interval/cron schedules are recurring. Use one-shot time only if that installed interface explicitly supports it. A clock targets an existing Home or Task run by ordinary binding, or authors an ordinary new run through its declared file-tool path. Set a concrete timestamp/timezone, reminder/context and one-shot/repeat semantics from the actual contract; no timer lives in Home or the kernel. Keep Home input independent of the time checkpoint. Disabling a schedule is its explicit config edit; stopping a Task or call must not silently disable it. Another event source follows the same exact interface/binding rule.

10. RECEIPT. Retain the generic file-write result for every changed record, the assignment emission verdict, subsequent artifact movements, and any verifier/mark evidence. Keep authored/admitted/consumed/completed/delivered/heard distinct. Do not fabricate a policy result from this example: the runtime forms and attests it from actual JSON. Report the precise failed contract when a write, role closure, provider, tool gate, verifier, reader or client surface is unavailable.

Every projected checkpoint requires an actual inbound interface binding. For artifact.send reach, author an exact-name provider-output checkpoint to the destination System pin and include the necessary readable worker-role closure. Its admitted vocabulary is the intended assignment or return label; ordinary provider/tool outputs do not satisfy that binding policy. Never author an active checkpoint without an inbound binding.

CLIENT PRESENTATION. A task display name belongs to its owning client interface, not its assignment prose or run identity. When native run creation exposes title, supply the requested task name there. Otherwise use the ordinary granted file-write tool to set the task client octopus_os.json presentation to {"name":"the requested task name","projects":[]}, preserving every other field. Names are exact nonempty single-line strings up to 80 characters. A task with its own worker configuration does not require a saved client Agent. To reuse a registered Agent, inspect its exact catalog worker/template/profile and select that template; do not claim a saved Agent identity for a new independent worker pin. Recheck the client metadata and actual result evidence before reporting completion.

authoring_examples.scope: Illustrative already-authored Task and Home frontiers showing explicit assignment and result movement. Provider/door/client lives, private file-writer checkpoints, role closure, EE records and policy ids must be composed from installed descriptors before execution. These records are schema examples, not an installed Home or an executable bootstrap template.

evidence_requirements: Use admitted file/tool artifacts and any required verifier outcomes.

payload.summary: A required capability is unavailable; no effect was claimed.
remaining_gaps: Exact missing interface/tool/path and required owner action belong here.

authoring_examples.receipt_claim: task.summary.received plus artifact_exists establishes readable artifact receipt. completed/blocked/failed is producer-authored content; it never becomes a success mark merely by arriving.

ArtifactBinding.description: POLICY.md §4 — an artifact binding is the run's authored declaration of its object-level rights on a specific artifact. The `id` names the artifact; the `access` states which of read/change/create/delete the run claims on it (default: read only — a bound artifact is readable context). Formation masks this down to the worker-interface + EE verb ceiling; the interface-binding (the default flow) is a separate axis on the checkpoint.

run_record_schema.derivation: document is an exact copy of the generated source schema. The exporter includes the status and nonblank run/checkpoint trace constraints enforced by validation_source. Cross-record identity, active checkpoint bindings, policy and registry references are validated by the actual candidate validator.
